<div class="section-kicker">What we do</div>

## Research built around decisions, not just data {.section-title}

Our work asks how spatial data and computational methods can help people make better decisions about **climate adaptation, migration, flooding, urban change, conservation, and environmental equity**. We work across the Great Lakes region, East Africa, and other rapidly changing landscapes, often in direct partnership with communities, planners, and public agencies.

<div class="card-grid">
<div class="topic-card"><h3>Climate adaptation & migration</h3><p>We study how climate hazards and migration may reshape cities and regions, and how communities can prepare before those changes arrive.</p><span class="tag">GLISA</span><span class="tag">CLARS</span><span class="tag">urban growth</span></div>
<div class="topic-card"><h3>Geospatial AI & urban analytics</h3><p>We use vision-language models, street-level imagery, remote sensing, and spatial machine learning to measure conditions that are difficult to observe at scale.</p><span class="tag">Detroit</span><span class="tag">VLMs</span><span class="tag">UrbanWORM</span></div>
<div class="topic-card"><h3>Participatory mapping & decision support</h3><p>We build interactive tools that combine local knowledge, community priorities, and environmental models in transparent planning workflows.</p><span class="tag">PIVOT</span><span class="tag">PPGIS</span><span class="tag">co-production</span></div>
<div class="topic-card"><h3>Landscape & conservation science</h3><p>We investigate how people perceive, value, and interact with landscapes using social media, spatial modeling, ecological data, and conservation science.</p><span class="tag">human–nature relationships</span><span class="tag">land change</span></div>
</div>

<div class="section-kicker">Featured</div>

## Current directions

**Great Lakes climate adaptation.** As Principal Investigator of GLISA, Derek Van Berkel leads research and engagement connecting climate science with communities and decision-makers across the Great Lakes.

**Climate migration across two lake regions.** CLARS links research in the Lake Victoria Basin and North American Great Lakes to understand migration, urban change, and climate knowledge exchange.

**AI for urban decision-making.** Work with the City of Detroit explores scalable analysis of residential property conditions using street-level imagery, vision-language models, and participatory planning tools.

**Flood resilience through co-production.** CHIRRP/PUMP-COR and PIVOT integrate hydrologic information, participatory GIS, and scenario planning to support community flood decisions.
